title: The rules as type
summary: The five rules as type (coherence pass 2, D5): the four [K] rules as run-in statements at 28px — title in --fg, its one-line gloss after it in --fg-2 — then the exit test as the page's poster line.
story: The doctrine, read rather than scanned: four rules in a paragraph's voice, the fifth set large because every engagement is designed backwards from it.
copy: [K] Diagnosis before prescription. “No engagement starts without the audit’s readout — building before diagnosing sells the same fix to every different problem.” (verbatim; whether ‘engagement’ should become ‘system’ is a founder question, now that projects run without the audit)

[K] Assets first — then the retainer. “Everything we install is documented in your language and lives in your stack. The operating retainer compounds a system you own — it never becomes the thing you rent.”
[R] Clarity is infrastructure. “Most pipeline problems are narrative problems in disguise. We write the language down first.” (round 8's [R] second sentence cut to fit the 120-word budget)
[R] Learning is the asset. “What an engagement learns is written into the system. Next quarter starts where this one ended.”
[K] The exit test (88px) — “If it stops working the day we leave, we built it wrong. Every engagement is designed backwards from this sentence.”
phone: ≤1023: the four keep two columns at 19px; the exit test 72px. ≤767: one column at 18px; the exit test at min(52px, 14% of the stage) on one line.

reference.site: Round-8 about-rules (the founder's words and the 88px exit-test poster moment, kept) · ROUND9-PLAN §2/§5
reference.borrowed: Editorial run-in heads: a name in the text's own voice running into its sentence, as in a printed manifesto.
reference.kelwin: No numbering (order is not the content), no ruled rows, no chips; one dominant line; graphite (the rules are not a paper document).

motion: entrance: the label fades, the four rise together, then the exit test rises and its sentence follows (the section's one moment).
notes: Coherence pass 2: no longer title-left/gloss-right rows (the row recipe stays on three pages only). 117 words at rest (label 5 · rules 112). Height ≈893px at 1440. No ruled list on the page now. Coherence pass (round 9): see summary. Coherence pass 3: rule 3's gloss no longer opens on “Most …”: “We write the language down first, because pipeline problems usually start in the narrative.” The exit test is set at the kit's claim size (.ac-claim--md: 64px at 1440, 48 tablets, 32 phones) so it never matches or outranks the h1 (it was 88 = the h1 at 1440, 72 > 69.5 at 834). Final check (verify r3): rule 3's gloss echoed the note title “why pipeline problems rarely start in the pipeline” (also the Insights index's first entry); now plainly: “We write the language down first, because every channel and sales call runs on it.” The rule title stays as approved.
